dimensions.note: The Anthropic key is marked `.meta({ sensitive: true })` in GlobalArgsSchema (retro.ts:138) and is meant to be supplied via a vault reference; it is never logged or written to a resource. Transcripts and digests are privacy-sensitive: they are written under `retroDir/digests/`, which the README documents as untracked, and only ledger.tsv/findings.md/batches are intended to be committed, with a redaction rule stated. No credential path.

Every logger call uses structured `{placeholder}` props (inventory totals, round counts, per-session names). No transcript text, prompt content, or the API key is interpolated into a log line. Failures log at error; completions at info.

Missing transcripts log and skip; missing `state`/`batch-NN` resources throw actionable messages naming the method to run. Post-review fix: `dirReadable` gates discovery so a transiently unreadable store root cannot mass-mark pending rows `lost`, and `synthesize` refuses to replace a non-empty register with an empty findings array. `callCommand` deliberately treats nonzero-exit-with-stdout as success because agent CLIs sometimes exit nonzero while still emitting a usable reply.

18 tests cover all three transcript adapters against fixtures shaped from real Claude Code, Codex, and Amp files; head+tail truncation; JSON extraction; ledger merge/refresh/scanned-runtime semantics; TSV round-trip; the Anthropic request shape and both error paths; Codex echo de-duplication; and an inventory->strip integration over a temp store. Note: the digest/synthesize model paths are not executed (they need a live provider); their prompt builders and schemas are exercised indirectly.

Post-review fixes: `inventory` is idempotent when there are no pending sessions (it writes the ledger only and does not advance the round or create an empty batch), and `markBatch` marks only the selected rows with the round (previously every pending row was stamped). Settled rows (digested/synthesized/skipped-subagent) keep their status across re-inventory, while in-flight/trivial rows are re-classified so they can become pending. `synthesize` marks only rows that produced a digest as synthesized.

Post-review fix: resource instance names are now unique per spec (`stripped-*`, `digest-*`, `batch-NN`, `round-NN`, plus `ledger`/`state`/`register`), removing cross-spec instance-name collisions that previously let a read parse another spec's schema. Every `writeResource` payload was enumerated and checked against its target schema. Deno.Command/Deno APIs are used in their documented forms.

`Deno.Command.output()` fully drains and closes pipes on every agent call; transcripts are read once and capped by `maxCharsPerSession` (head+tail elision) before prompt assembly; no temp files or open handles are left. Note: a single very large transcript is materialized before the cap is applied — bounded in practice by session-file size, not a leak.

The manifest ships only the model, README, and LICENSE. No test fixtures, runtime data, personal hostnames, tokens, or account identifiers appear in the published surface; README examples use generic paths.

All schemas are strict `z.object` with no passthrough. Post-review fix: digest identity fields (runtime/sessionId/scope) are applied after the model output so a reply cannot spoof them, and the register cannot be emptied by a stray empty findings array.

High-churn `stripped` uses 30d/20; append-only `digest`, `round`, `register`, `recommendation`, `ledger`, and `state` are infinite with per-spec garbage collection. Distinct factory instances accumulate but are bounded per spec by the GC setting.

The six methods cover the full pixel-to-register pipeline. There is no externally CRUD-managed entity; the register is a projection the model owns, so create/read/update are all present and no delete is meaningful (findings retire rather than delete).

No `checks` block by design: a provider/dependency check would block the non-LLM `inventory` and `strip` methods that need no key. Methods instead fail fast with actionable errors when required resources are absent. A future `retro-config` check could validate provider settings without a dependency label.

Post-review fix: `strippedResName`/`digestResName`/`batchResName`/`roundResName` prefix each spec's instances, and `ledger`/`state`/`register` are singletons. Session ids are truncated to 8 hex chars for readability; collisions would require two sessions sharing the first 8 chars of a UUID, and both runtime and scope are also stored on the resource.

Post-review fix: every `readResource` name matches how it was written (state; batch-NN; stripped-*; digest-*; register; ledger). No direct dataRepository access; all state flows through writeResource/readResource, so CEL consumers see the same shapes.
manifest.yaml `2026.10.11.1` matches `model.version`. No upgrades entries are needed for a first publish; a future global-argument or resource-schema change must add an `upgrades` entry.

mechanical.schema-write-conformance: pass — all 8 resource writers verified against their schemas: ledger (LedgerSchema), state (StateSchema), batch (BatchSchema), stripped (StrippedSchema), digest (DigestSchema), register (RegisterSchema), round (RoundSchema), recommendation (RecommendationSchema). No placeholder or partial writes.
mechanical.resource-name-uniqueness: FIXED — stripped and digest previously shared `sessionName()` instance names, and batch and round previously shared `round-NN`. Both collisions were removed with per-spec prefixes (`stripped-*`, `digest-*`, `batch-NN`, `round-NN`).
mechanical.batch-selection-bug: FIXED — `inventory` previously stamped every pending ledger row with the new round via `assignBatch(merged, round)`; it now marks only the selected batch rows via `markBatch(merged, selected, round)`.
mechanical.false-lost-guard: FIXED — a store root that is missing or unreadable no longer causes all of its previously pending rows to be marked `lost`; `discover()` reports which runtimes were actually scanned and `mergeLedger` only marks `lost` for those.
mechanical.provider-abstraction: pass — `provider: anthropic` posts directly to the Messages API; `provider: command` pipes the composed prompt to a user-supplied shell command on stdin and reads stdout, enabling cross-vendor (e.g. codex) quota relief. Both paths are configuration, not hard-coded vendor logic.
mechanical.privacy-posture: pass — digests are written under `retroDir/digests/` and documented as untracked; evidence quotes are capped at 25 words in the rubric; the README states the redaction obligation for committed files.
